ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners and signatories against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (ii) the South African domestic financial sanctions list administered by the Financial Intelligence Centre, (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list wherever USD payment rails are used, and (iv) the FATF high-risk jurisdiction list; foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs / prominent influential persons under the expanded FICA definition) trigger enhanced due diligence, senior management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring; adverse media and negative-news searches are customary for bank KYC and FICA compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eservices national portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za and https://biz.gov.za) using Form CoR 9.1 (Notice of Reservation of a Company Name)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin-alphabet characters in English or Afrikaans; non-Latin scripts (including Chinese characters) are rejected and a 1:1 Romanized transliteration is mandatory; the proposed name must not be the same as or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark, must not be 'undesirable' within the meaning of section 11(2)(b) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and must not falsely imply official or state sponsorship.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Building Society, Insurance, Assurance, Financial Services (prior Prudential Authority / FSCA approval required)
Stock Exchange, Securities, Clearing House (Financial Sector Conduct Authority approval required)
Medical, Hospital, Clinic, Pharmacy (Health Professions Council of South Africa approval required)
University, College, School, Education (Department of Higher Education and Training approval required)
South Africa, Government, President, Minister, Parliament, Municipal, Police (ministerial approval under sections 11(2)(c) and 11(3) of the Companies Act required)
Holding, Holdings, Group (triggers group-relationship declaration requirements under section 11(4) of the Companies Act)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 business days of a name-rejection notice, the applicant may lodge Form CTR 142 with the Companies Tribunal under section 160(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requesting a determination that the proposed name does not contravene the Act; the Companies Tribunal must decide the matter within 60 business days of referral and may substitute its own order permitting registration. Alternatively, the applicant may file a fresh CoR 9.1 with a modified distinctive element or request direct CIPC reconsideration where the rejection is based on a curable defect. Judicial review under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 remains available in the High Court as a final remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the statutory registered office at incorporation subject to section 23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, which mandates a physical serviceable address in South Africa accessible to the public during business hours; a mailbox-only virtual address satisfies the strict letter of the statute but is commercially inadvisable for a refractory-masonry contractor because banks, the SARS VAT branch and industrial clients will require an operational executive address or tendering presence; a serviced virtual office with physical reception and site-contact details is accepted by CIPC and FICA for a low-risk ISIC 4329 contracting entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of 15% within the first 12 months: unannounced CIPC loco-compliance inspections targeting registered offices occur in approximately 2-5% of low-risk private companies per annum and are triggered primarily by complaints or suspected fraud; however, once on-site boiler and kiln refractory works commence, Department of Employment and Labour construction-site health-and-safety inspections are near-certain (90% or higher over a 12-month contract period) and will separately verify registered-office records and director identity during the principal-contractor safety-file audit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 8(2)(b), 13–15, 19, 23, 24(2), 27, 66, 70–72 and 76; Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R351) Part H; General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combatting Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022, s 26 (beneficial-ownership disclosure); Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 for SARS registration obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), acting through the CIPC e-Services online portal at https://eservices.cipc.co.za.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (standard-form election CoR 14.1A or bespoke MOI), first-director consents, and the CIPC beneficial-ownership disclosure.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued capital is prescribed for a private company; a (Pty) Ltd may be incorporated with one or more shares of any par value or of no par value, and no escrow account, capital deposit or proof of paid-up capital is required. The only statutory constraint is the prohibition in s 8(2)(b) on offering shares to the public.

FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at 1st Floor, 15 Alice Lane, Sandton, Johannesburg, 2196, and that the Company Secretary file the registered-office notice with CIPC under section 23. FURTHER RESOLVED that Johan van der Merwe be appointed sole Director, Thandi Nkosi Company Secretary, and Pieter Botha prescribed officer for health, safety and environmental compliance, each consenting to act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Beneficial-Ownership Pre-Filing Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC registration eServices module; run the company name search engine; submit a name-reservation application for up to three names in priority order (CoR 9.1 in manual lodgement, or the online name-reservation transaction); pay the prescribed electronic search and reservation fee; retain the reservation reference number, which is valid for six months; confirm the proposed name is not identical, offensive or unduly similar to a registered company name or trademark.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document or passport of each incorporator, subscriber and proposed director
Name-reservation application setting out up to three proposed names
Proof of payment of the CIPC name-search and reservation fee
Power of attorney of the submitting agent, if filed through a registered CIPC practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the name is declined administratively, file a name objection or apply to the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for reconsideration; an alternative reserved name may be carried into the Notice of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing – Notice of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation and First Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1); elect the standard MOI (CoR 14.1A) or upload a bespoke MOI approved by the incorporators; insert the reserved company name, registered office, postal address, financial year-end, first directors and company secretary, together with their signed consents to act; attach the beneficial-ownership disclosure; pay the prescribed filing fee; upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3) and the CIPC-certified Memorandum of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Standard-form MOI election (CoR 14.1A) or bespoke Memorandum of Incorporation
Signed consent-to-act forms for each first director and the company secretary
Certified IDs or passports of incorporators, directors and secretary
Proof of payment of the CIPC filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a defect or correction request, amend the CoR 14.1 or MOI within the stated defect period and re-upload with the prescribed resubmission fee; a refusal grounded on name or MOI legality may be appealed to the Companies Tribunal under s 160.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration and Compliance Profile with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an organisation profile on SARS eFiling; register the company for income tax and provisional tax; apply for VAT registration where the taxable turnover exceeds or is reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1 million in any 12-month period; once employees are engaged, register for PAYE, UIF and Skills Development Levy; submit the company registration data; print the SARS registration acknowledgment and record the official income tax reference number.
required_dossiers: CIPC-certified extract of the Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents of the authorised directors
Company bank account confirmation for refund routing
Utility or lease proof of the registered and trading address
Declared expected turnover for the VAT registration threshold
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS places the registration in a verification or non-active status, resubmit the outstanding supporting records within 21 business days; any unwarranted refusal or penalty may be objected to under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 through the SARS eFiling disputes workflow.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; statutory mandate under the South African Revenue Service Act 34 of 1997 and the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate via the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) using Form CoR 14.1 to obtain the company registration number. Step 2: Register on SARS eFiling to obtain the Income Tax Reference Number (auto-populated through CIPC-SARS data exchange or via a SARS branch/online application). Step 3: File VAT101 application with SARS where taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 per annum (compulsory) or exceed ZAR 50,000 (voluntary). Step 4: Obtain a SARS Customs Client Code (Customs Code) for import/export clearance. Step 5: Register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), UIF and SDL via eFiling where employees are engaged. Step 6: Appoint a public officer resident in South Africa under s246 TAA responsible for tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A South African (Pty) Ltd is a tax resident company (incorporated and subject to domestic legal form under the Companies Act 71 of 2008) taxed on worldwide income at the 27% corporate income tax rate for tax years ending on or after 31 March 2023; capital gains included at an 80% inclusion rate (effective 21.6%); distributions subject to 20% dividends tax; no pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; a (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily entity-level taxed. Elective regimes available: (i) Small Business Corporation (s12E) progressive rates of 0%, 7%, 21%, 27% on taxable income up to ZAR 550,000, available only where all shareholders are natural persons and no non-resident company holds more than 5% shareholding; (ii) Micro Business Turnover Tax (s48A-s48F) up to ZAR 1,000,000 turnover; (iii) VAT group registration (s50 VAT Act) for 51% related entities; (iv) Corporate restructure roll-over elections under s45, s46 and s47 Income Tax Act; (v) s11D research and development allowance election upon prior SARS/DTI approval; (vi) hybrid mismatch neutralisation elections under s12N effective 1 January 2024 aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) imposed under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 (VAT Act), administered by SARS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory registration threshold for annual taxable supplies, s23(1) VAT Act); ZAR 50,000 (voluntary registration threshold, s24(1) VAT Act).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS has not yet implemented mandatory real-time fiscal clearance/CTC with digital stamping; however, the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 and VAT Act s20 mandate complete original tax invoices for all standard-rated and zero-rated supplies, issued within 21 days of the supply date and retained for 5 years. Electronic tax invoices (PDF/XML) are accepted where integrity and accessibility standards under SARS Interpretation Note 53 are met. Customs obligations are fully electronic via SARS Customs EDI/eFiling, requiring electronic filing of SAD500 declarations, and a multi-year mandatory e-invoicing programme is included in the SARS digital roadmap.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to a non-SACU 'export country' qualify for 0% VAT where the supplier exports the goods (s11(1)(a) VAT Act) or the buyer/agent exports them within 90 days of supply (s11(1)(c)); services supplied to non-residents not present in South Africa at the time of supply qualify under s11(2)(k) where not directly connected with land or movable property in South Africa. Claims require retention of export shipment evidence and extension of zero-rated status with the statutory reason stated on the tax invoice; SACU member state supplies (Botswana, Lesotho, Eswatini, Namibia) do not qualify unless special exclusions apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SAD500 Customs Export Declaration (approved via SARS Customs EDI/eFiling or freight forwarder consolidation report)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export to a non-SACU destination
Original commercial invoice (zero-rated, quoting s11(1)(a) or s11(1)(c) of the VAT Act)
Packing list and cargo manifest matching goods description, weights, and quantities
International transport/supply contract and proof of delivery (POD)
Proof of inward payment: SWIFT MT103 / foreign currency remittance advice (inward foreign investment allowance or modernised RCA record)
Non-resident customer identity documentation and destination confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating cannot be substantiated or goods are diverted inside South Africa, SARS invokes the s16(3)(c) VAT Act clawback, raising additional VAT (output tax) with interest at the prescribed rate (s28 VAT Act / s187 TAA). Understatement penalties under s222/s223 TAA escalate from 10% (no culpable conduct) to 25% (not substantially in the dark), 50% (substantial understatement), 75% (lack of reasonable care) and 150% (intentional tax evasion); fraudulent export claims are further subject to criminal prosecution under s234 TAA (fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years for repeat offenders). Failure to timeously repatriate export proceeds within 180 days triggers SARB Exchange Control default reporting, administrative financial penalties, and criminal sanctions under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), Exchange Control Division
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is classified as a designated currency with full convertibility on the current account, including trade-related payments, dividends, interest, and royalties, subject to documentation review by an Authorised Dealer (AD). Capital account transactions are regulated under the South African Exchange Control Regulations: non-resident direct equity investments are freely convertible inward, but liberalisation requires formal reporting through an Authorised Dealer, and exits, adverse dividend flows, or repatriation of capital may require FinSurv statistical declarations. Profit remittance is permitted without prior SARB approval provided SARS tax clearance status verifies that the distribution is from taxed local profits and the corporate law requirements (Companies Act, Memorandum of Incorporation, board resolution) are complied with. However, the burden lies on the South African entity to evidence the underlying transaction, maintain proper BOP codes, and retain all source documents for six years. Cross-border funding through foreign shareholder loans is also permitted, but must be declared and may be subject to thin capitalisation and treasury anti-abuse scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under South African Exchange Control Regulations, export proceeds for goods shipped from South Africa must be received in full within 180 days of the date of shipment unless an extension is approved (maximum practical extension is 365 days in limited circumstances). All foreign currency export proceeds must be surrendered to an Authorised Dealer within 30 days of receipt and converted into ZAR at the prevailing market rate, unless the exporter has obtained an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or special exemption. The mandatory conversion ratio for ordinary trade receipts is effectively 100% of the export invoice amount, net of permitted deductions (commission, freight, insurance). The Authorised Dealer is required to obtain the relevant export documentation (customs AD480 bill of entry, commercial invoice, proof of shipment, sale contract) and to verify that the remitting bank and payment tenor are consistent with Exchange Control Circulars.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM (2.5/5) as a standalone treasury rail. Offshore Electronic Money Institution (EMI) accounts are generally not recognised as Authorised Dealer bank accounts under South African exchange control and cannot serve as the principal receiving account for direct inward investments, export proceeds, or mandatory SARB reporting. They may be used as ancillary collection/payment tools for low-value disbursements, but they create income tax, VAT, and marketable securities reporting friction, and the SARB Foreign Exchange Guidelines discourage routing of cross-border trade through third-party payment processors not holding a South African bank licence. Any use of an offshore EMI for employee expense reimbursement or operational petty cash must be fully reconciled in the company's ZAR books and must not obscure the statutory BOP reporting trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) requires the bank to verify the identity of all natural persons who are directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners of the legal entity. In practice, the typical corporate account onboarding process requires at least one responsible officer, preferably a director with executive authority, to attend an in-person interview at the bank branch or to complete a notarised/virtual ID verification with an Authorised Dealer where the bank's risk appetite permits. For a shareholder/director located outside South Africa, the bank will usually accept a certified copy of the passport, an apostilled power of attorney, and a live video verification only if the account signatory appears through a secure link and the bank can validate biometric or identity-document details. Remote opening is possible for select banks when the entire board is non-resident, but almost all Tier 1 banks revert to a physical attendance requirement for the final execution of mandates and the activation of foreign-currency and capital escrow facilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directorship and opaque ownership chain; ultimate beneficial owner located in a jurisdiction flagged as high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies of all directors; a detailed corporate ownership chart showing each intermediate holding company up to the ultimate natural person; registered shareholder register from CIPC; bank confirmation of non-embargoed status; a sworn affidavit on the source of capital; and independent sanctions/PEPSI screening output from a reputable compliance provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth cannot be evidenced from South African banking records for the inbound capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or bank-verified financial statements of the ultimate shareholder for the latest two years; tax returns or tax clearance certificates of the investor; loan or share subscription agreements with clear payment terms; SWIFT MT103 advisories showing the original remitter account in a low-risk jurisdiction; and a signed declaration that the funds are not derived from criminal proceeds or circumvention of sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade pattern / sector disconnect: a small construction/refractory-masonry entity receiving unusually large or rapid foreign funding before the underlying kiln-installation contract is substantiated.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts, purchase orders, or letters of intent for the South African industrial boiler/refractory lining project; detailed project cash-flow forecast; progress billing schedule; certificate from the client or project engineer confirming work commencement; and third-party procurement or vendor invoice evidence supporting the intended expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP alerts on invoicing counterparties, subcontractors, or suppliers in the boiler maintenance supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full end-to-end sanctions screening output for all counterparties with a clear risk classification; beneficial ownership declarations from suppliers; transaction-specific letters explaining the commercial nexus; and a compliance escalation memo submitted through the bank's AML/KYC portal with prior error or false-positive resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to provide SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN or unresolved South African revenue obligations at the entity/beneficial owner level.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Tax Clearance Status (TCS) PIN for the (Pty) Ltd; tax clearance certificates for the direct and ultimate shareholders, if available; a SARS statement of account showing no outstanding returns or liabilities; and, where applicable, a confirmed deferral/instalment arrangement with SARS before the account opening decision.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing of an inbound foreign equity subscription or shareholder loan to ZA_PTY_LTD is executed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent/remitter's bank to the Account with Bank. The payment message must carry a clear remittance reference to the underlying share subscription or loan agreement and the South African Balance of Payments code (BOP code) for direct investment (e.g., FA 3001 for direct investment equity, or FA 3010 for direct investment loans where applicable). The Authorised Dealer will verify the purpose, check the beneficiary's FICA/KYC file, confirm SARS TCS status, and obtain the appropriate Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) reporting; typical documentary evidence includes the board resolution approving allotment of shares, the completed Form ABC (Advance Receipt of Funds), capital subscription agreement, investor due diligence pack, and where the foreign shareholder is a company, the certified extract of incumbency and ownership certificate. The bank will then credit the operational/capital escrow account in ZAR at the prevailing spot rate and produce a Foreign Exchange Transaction Advice (FETA) and a BOP return for SARB. Any currency conversion must occur only with an Authorised Dealer, and any intended use of the funds for project expenses must be supported by contractual invoices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for refractory lining projects, subcontractor procurement, and equipment purchases are cleared primarily through the ZAR domestic clearing system (SAMOS - South African Multiple Option Settlement) for local payments, while cross-border trade settlements use SWIFT MT103s for outright supplier payments and documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) under UCP 600 for import or performance guarantee structures. Each cross-border USD/EUR/GBP payment must be accompanied by the relevant BOP code (e.g., 3020 for imports, 3001 for dividend repatriation), the underlying contract, commercial invoice, and verification of SARB Form A or equivalent declaration. Where funds are in a foreign currency account, the Authorised Dealer may process direct foreign-currency settlement without conversion, provided the outflow is coded and approved. Payments to high-risk or sanctions-affected jurisdictions are blocked unless a successful advisory from the bank's sanctions team is received. Treasury staff should ensure the use of irrevocable LBUs only via the bank's electronic system and retain MT103 evidence for transfer pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) in USD/EUR/GBP/ZAR matched to underlying export receivable or import payable, with a fixed tenor not exceeding trade settlement cycle.
Cross-currency swap (CCS) with an Authorised Dealer to hedge foreign-currency funding and repayment obligations over the life of the project.
Currency interest-rate swap (CIRS) under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement for long-term project financing exposure.
Plain-vanilla OTC currency call/put options economically linked to contracted trade flows, entered into with a licensed South African bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not available to onshore resident corporates for managing ZAR risk; offshore NDF hedging may be considered only through a licensed offshore subsidiary and with written Exchange Control approval, as South African corporates are expected to use deliverable forwards through Authorised Dealers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (incorporated annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty accrues for every year of arrears; two consecutive years of outstanding annual returns trigger deregistration or administrative strike-off under section 82(4)(b) of Companies Act 71 of 2008

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) including audit or independent review report as applicable, tabled before shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; CIPC on statutory request or as part of annual return compliance for qualifying entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and table AFS within 6 months is an offence; CIPC may issue a compliance notice and directors may be penalized or disqualified for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register maintenance and annual confirmation event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC through the annual return filing process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation aligns with the annual return deadline; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 5 business days after the company becomes aware of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or inaccurate submission of beneficial ownership data is a criminal offence carrying an unlimited fine and/or imprisonment under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit is mandatory when the public interest score equals or exceeds 350, or if the entity is a public, state-owned, or listed company; private companies with a public interest score of 100 to 349 require an independent review unless shareholders resolve to have a full audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS; IFRS for SMEs may be used by qualifying private companies with limited public accountability, as permitted under the Companies Act 71 of 2008

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return to CIPC constitutes the annual confirmation that the beneficial ownership register is complete and accurate. A company must maintain a register of beneficial interests in the prescribed form and lodge any changes to CIPC within 5 business days of learning of the change or registrable event
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Members' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,500 - 15,000 for full audit; 1,500 - 4,500 for independent review

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
